summary: Umpqua NF summit in Lane County, OR: a 1920s pole platform, then a 1949 L-4 tower removed in 1967; the Forest Service says the stone foundation remains.

facts.design: 30-foot wooden tower with an L-4 cab (1949), after a 1934 cabin and a 1920s 50-foot pole platform
facts.status_note: Tower removed or destroyed in 1967; the Forest Service says the stone foundation remains on the summit

staffing.status: classed as an emergency station in August 1962

access.note: Reached by the Forest Service Mount June Trail, a hiking route that links to the Sawtooth Trail

visit.trail_note: Hike the Mount June Trail to the summit, where the stone foundation of the old lookout remains

events.note: Placeholder year for the 1920s: sources give only the decade for the 50-foot pole platform
Late-1925 newspaper items (26 Nov and 4 Dec) said the peak would probably be designated a forest fire lookout point
Cabin quarters, an L-4 hip-roofed lookout house, built on the summit
Cabin quarters replaced by a 30-foot wooden tower with an L-4 cab; the Forest Service trail page says 50 feet
Classed as an emergency station in an August 1962 News-Review item quoted on the Oregon lookouts page
Register and Oregon lookouts page say removed; firelookout.com says destroyed; Forest Service says all structures abandoned and destroyed

evidence.supports: 50-foot pole platform in the 1920s; cabin 1934; 30-foot L-4 tower 1949; removed 1967
evidence.quote: The first lookout on this site was a 50' pole platform built in the 1920s. Cabin quarters were built in 1934 and were replaced in 1949 with a 30' wooden L-4 tower, which was removed in 1967.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com, the Oregon lookouts page and the Friends of the Umpqua all give 30 feet (9.1 m) for the 1949 tower; the Forest Service trail page says 50 feet. The record keeps 30 feet, the figure most sources give, and the story names both.
Three sources say the tower was removed in 1967; firelookout.com and the Forest Service page say destroyed. The story says it came down and uses both words.
